page: Amazon Web Services p3dn.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, engineered specifically for distributed machine learning training and deep learning inference. The host configuration pairs an Intel Xeon 8175M processor featuring 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz with 768 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs delivering a collective 256 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. In addition, the instance bundles 1,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and establishes 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across parallelized and GPU-driven workloads. LLM inference metrics register in the top 10 percent across prompt processing and generation for both medium 7B and large 70B parameter models. Multi-core performance is similarly robust, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 55,735.65 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 80,918.99. In-memory operations also reflect substantial capacity, clocking 75.0 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 217.49 GB/sec of uncached read memory bandwidth. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression place in the lower quartile, reflecting the architectural bias toward broad parallel scaling over per-core clock speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance consolidates substantial GPU density, high memory capacity, and 100 Gbps networking into a single machine. While instances of this scale represent substantial operational commitments, the dense aggregation of eight Volta GPUs alongside 1.8 TB of bundled local NVMe storage reduces inter-node communication overhead in multi-GPU distributed pipelines. The p3dn.24xlarge is well tailored for large language model inference, large-scale deep learning model training, high-throughput distributed parameter serving, and GPU-accelerated scientific simulations.
